feeds.note: The FINEST flat row (#410), for the 0.6 mm corn cutter; appended so a 0.8 mm cutter still takes the 0.8-1.6 mm row.
feeds.provenance: PLACEHOLDER, nothing measured: the 0.8-1.6 mm row's own starting values (S12000, F500, F200 — the Z1's emitted defaults) with the step-down and step-over cut back for a 0.6 mm cutter, which is the least stiff bit the bench owns. No vendor row for this diameter. #284 measures it.

From the 2026-10-15 bench cut (#185, `docs/bench/185-v-groove.nc`): the hand file's own numbers — S12000, F500 along, F200 plunge, one pass to depth — cut a clean V groove in PLA (0.836 mm opening at 1.0 mm deep, the 30° × 0.3 mm bit). Starting values, not a coupon measurement: #284 is what measures this row.

OBSERVED 2026-10-17, not measured: the 30° × 0.3 mm V-bit ran PETG at S12000, F500 along, F200 plunge for 856 s without melting. The numbers are the PLA V row's own starting values; no coupon measured PETG, and this row is a chosen placeholder for the two-colour blank. #284 is what settles it.

feeds.note: Laminate V row (#450): the 0.3-0.5 mm band; only the feed was swept, rpm/plunge/step-down are the PLA V row carried over.
feeds.provenance: Measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (Dave) on the purchased two-colour laminate 76 x 25.35 x 1.5 with the yellow Single Flute Engraving Bit 30 deg x 0.3 mm: four cells F400/F600/F800/F1000 at S12000, F200 plunge, 0.1 mm deep, all clean by eye (no melt, no strings); chose 1000. Record docs/bench/450-laminate-v-feed-coupon-record.json, photo docs/bench/img/2026-10-18-laminate-V-feed-coupon.jpg.

adaptive.cutFeed.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the adaptive clearing feed until a measured row replaces it

adaptive.engagementFraction.note: chosen, not measured: the most new material a clearing move may take per mm of travel, as a fraction of the cutter diameter

adaptive.entryClearanceMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far above the floor just cut a rapid down a cleared column stops, and the clearance every entry starts from

adaptive.entryFeed.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the helix and ramp entry feed until a measured row replaces it

adaptive.helixDiameterFraction.note: chosen, not measured: the helix entry's diameter as a fraction of the cutter diameter; the helix is refused where its bore does not fit

adaptive.maxCells.note: chosen, not measured: the largest material grid adaptive clearing will build; a pocket needing more cells at the planned engagement is refused rather than ground through

adaptive.neckAreaMm2.note: chosen, not measured: material in a neck narrower than the grid can see, above this area, refuses the plan rather than being left standing

adaptive.rampAngleDeg.note: chosen, not measured: the descent angle of the helix and ramp entries

adaptive.residualShare.note: chosen, not measured: the material adaptive clearing may leave as grid noise along the walls, as a share of the area to clear

adaptive.spindleRpm.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the adaptive spindle speed until a measured row replaces it

adaptive.stepDownMm.note: chosen, not measured: the deepest level adaptive clearing cuts at once

bracket.armLengthXMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera L Bracket, inside corner to the end of the scale arm (both arms 85)

bracket.armLengthYMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera L Bracket, inside corner to the end of the other arm (both arms 85)

bracket.armWidthMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera L Bracket arm, stock face to outside face

bracket.fitMm.note: default, not measured: how closely a corner pushed into the bracket repeats (the design's +/-0.1)

bracket.heightMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera L Bracket, underside to top; the M5 heads sit in counterbores

bracket.originOffsetXMm.note: default, not measured: the stock's corner in the bracket from anchor 1 along X. 0 is Makera's own (Z1 QuickStart: work origin relative to Anchor 1, X offset 0); caliper the bracket's inside face to the anchor

bracket.originOffsetYMm.note: default, not measured: the stock's corner in the bracket from anchor 1 along Y. 0 is Makera's own (Z1 QuickStart: Y offset 0); caliper the bracket's inside face to the anchor

bracket.repeatMm.note: provisional, not measured: how closely a bracket seated on the anchor pins repeats; #208 B1 owes the pin-to-face measurement

clamp.refuseFraction.note: chosen, not measured: the band above the machine's feed/rpm ceiling where a value is refused rather than clamped

clamps.topHeightMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera Top Clamp 5.05 thick + a standard M5 cap-screw head 5.0; the nose steps down to 3.6 and 1.05 (docs/bench/img/2026-10-18-top-clamp-stepped-nose.jpg)

clamps.topInFromCornerMm.note: chosen placement, not a measurement: a clamp's side this far in from the corner of the edge it holds

clamps.topLengthMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera Top Clamp Set, end to end along the slot

clamps.topReachMm.note: default, not measured: how far a top clamp's nose reaches in over the stock from its edge

clamps.topWidthMm.note: measured 2026-10-18 by the maintainer (calipers, DAVE-1 bench): Makera Top Clamp Set, across the slot

console.firstReplyMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long a typed console line waits for its first reply. Above the slowest lines timed on the bench (M491 about 32 s, $H about 31 s, 2026-10-15)

console.maxMs.note: chosen, not measured: the longest a console reply may run; never shorter than the first-reply wait

console.quietMs.note: chosen, not measured: the quiet gap that ends a console reply

drill.peckClearanceMm.note: chosen, not measured: after a peck the drill rapids back down to this far above the floor it just cut

drill.peckDiameters.note: chosen, not measured: each peck goes this many drill diameters deep before the drill retracts to clear chips

drill.plungeFeed.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the drilling feed until a measured row replaces it

drill.pointAngleDeg.note: chosen, not measured: a twist drill's included point angle, used only when the drill's own record states none

drill.spindleRpm.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the drilling spindle speed until a measured row replaces it

engrave.blankBandFill.note: chosen, not measured: how much of a free band the seeded line takes, as a share of it; more fill means a taller cap and less clearance

engrave.lostDetailWarnRatio.note: chosen, not measured: the share of an item's area a cutter must reach before the item is called detail-lost

engrave.newDrillDepthMm.note: chosen, not measured: the depth a new hole starts at — deeper than an item's own starting depth because a hole that shallow shows nothing on the preview

engrave.newItemDepthMm.note: chosen, not measured: the depth a new label, shape, combined shape, traced line or imported outline starts at, in the panel where the person then sets the depth that matters

engrave.newThreadDepthMm.note: chosen, not measured: the threaded length a new thread item starts at

facing.marginMm.note: chosen, not measured: added to a probed top's high-to-low spread to fill in the facing depth, so the skim clears the highest point of the face

facing.retouchToleranceMm.note: chosen, not measured: the +/- band around the top a facing skim was posted to leave; the post-facing re-touch accepts a measurement inside it, because a skim never removes exactly its nominal depth

facing.roughMm.note: chosen, not measured: the facing depth filled in for rough stock — the heavy end of the 0.2 to 0.5 mm skim general practice uses; the person is asked and can change it

facing.unknownMm.note: chosen, not measured: the facing depth filled in when the stock's finish is unknown — the light end of the same 0.2 to 0.5 mm skim

finish.stockToLeaveMm.note: chosen, not measured: how much stock the roughing pass leaves on the walls and the floor for the finishing pass. 0.2 mm is about one printed layer at the common layer height. The first bench cut that inspects a finished floor replaces this

house.requestTimeoutMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long a house service request gets before it is called dead; a service on this machine or LAN answers in single-digit milliseconds, and the client compiled 2 s

import.dxfChordToleranceMm.note: chosen, not measured: the most a flattened DXF arc may stray from the true arc; smaller is more points

import.traceDespecklePx.note: chosen, not measured: the smallest ink blob or enclosed hole kept, in pixels of the source image; smaller specks are dropped before tracing

import.traceSimplifyPx.note: chosen, not measured: how far a traced boundary's pixel staircase may be straightened, in pixels of the source image

import.traceThreshold.note: chosen, not measured: the luminance a traced pixel must be darker than to count as ink; 0 to 255

laser.originUncertaintyMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far the laser dot's origin may be from the stock's corner (the dot's size, and its offset from the spindle axis, are not measured); point-to-origin is refused for a job whose edge margin is tighter

machine.connectTimeoutMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long a TCP connect to the machine's command port may take before it is called unreachable; the bridge compiled 3 s

machine.discoveryWindowMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long the app listens for the machine's UDP broadcast before deciding it is not announcing itself; the protocol compiled 3 s

machine.identifyWindowMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long each reply to the identify asks (M482.5, then M482.4) is waited for; the protocol compiled 1.5 s

machine.uploadInactivityMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long an upload waits for the machine's next frame before it cancels the transfer; the protocol compiled 9 s

margins.boundaryMarginMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far every floor stays clear of a plane it must not cross; 0.2 is one printed layer at the common layer height. While it is the seed, a blank that states its print uses its own layer height instead

margins.breakthroughMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far a through-cut may pass below the part's underside; seeds each new job

margins.edgeMarginMm.note: chosen, not measured: how close an item may come to a stock edge; seeds each new job

margins.jawClearanceMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far a cut's floor must stay above the vise jaws' tops; seeds each new job

margins.measuredThicknessToleranceMm.note: not measured: the +/- a caliper-measured stock thickness adds to a job's Z budget; provisional until the bench measures it (#208)

margins.minFloorMm.note: chosen, not measured: material that must remain under the deepest cut; seeds each new job, which then owns its own value

margins.zToleranceMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far this machine is expected to put the blank and the registration out in Z; a job's recommendation adds the blank's own dome to it

offcut.minSideMm.note: chosen, not measured: an offcut is offered back to the shelf only when both its sides are at least this (Q3: only leftover stock that has some size to it)

offcut.offer.note: chosen, not measured: offer an offcut back to the shelf at the end of a run that split the stock (false: never ask)

plan.autoLevelPointSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: one auto-level point; an estimate until #176 runs a grid here

plan.autoLevelPoints.note: chosen, not measured: the auto-level grid's point count, Makera Studio's own 3 x 3 default

plan.autoLevelShallowMm.note: chosen, not measured: on stock not known flat, a cut shallower than this wants an auto-level grid (Makera Studio's own rule)

plan.clearanceSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: the vacuum off and the clearance move after a cut (observed, not timed)

plan.finishSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: the end of a job, M332, spindle off, G28 (observed, not timed)

plan.fitCutterSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: fitting a cutter by hand at a bit change, from the plan of section 5.8; the first timed run replaces it

plan.fitProbeSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: fitting the wired probe by hand, from the plan of section 5.8; the first timed run replaces it

plan.homeSeconds.note: the mean of the five $H homes in the 2026-10-15 console trace: 27.0, 27.7, 29.4, 22.3 and 31.2 s (send to reply, 16:55, 17:14, 17:25, 19:14, 23:37)

plan.toolLengthSeconds.note: the four complete M491 tool-length touches on the wired probe in the 2026-10-15 console trace, sent to Done ATC: 31.36, 31.25, 32.18 and 31.35 s (16:34, 16:55, 17:15, 18:53); a fifth at 18:58 ended early and is not counted

plan.touchSeconds.note: chosen, not measured as the app's runner would take it: 15 s a touch, from the 2026-10-15 console trace's edge scans, driven by a console script, not the app runner. 32 touch-to-touch intervals under 20 s (G38.2 Z-5, 16:35:59 to 16:50:34): median 13.3 s, mean 14.0 s, range 10.4 to 19.7 s; the round trips between touches are included

power.cyclePauseSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: how long a plug cycle leaves the machine off before switching it on again (power.sh on --cycle)

power.pollSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: the wait between checks while switching on waits for the controller to answer

power.probeGapSeconds.note: chosen, not measured: the wait between those probes

power.probeTries.note: chosen, not measured: how many machine probes, all silent, before a powered machine counts as not answering (#416 review: one silent probe is a Wi-Fi blip as often as a dead controller)

registration.chuckAxisResidualMm.note: provisional, not measured: the chuck's runout where it locates the axis; #208 owes the bench measurement

registration.idlePollLimit.note: chosen, not measured: how many status polls the registration waits for Idle before a touch, about a second each, before it stops

registration.probeResidualMm.note: assumed, not measured: the 3D probe's ball-contact scatter in X, Y and Z, and what is left after a touch. The wired probe measured 0.001 mm in Z (registration.wiredProbeZResidualMm); this stays the conservative figure until the 3D probe is measured the same way (2026-10-08, /Z1-Firmware-Dialect.md §11.7)

registration.readingResolutionMm.note: chosen, not measured: the depth two touch readings are told apart by (the machine's dial, not the probe's spec)

registration.scanMissMarginMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far past the jaw tops a run-sheet scan touch may travel before it is called nothing; the cap that keeps a touch with nothing under it off the bed

registration.surfaceSlowSeekMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far the slow surface touch may travel. It starts 1 mm above the fast touch's hit, so it must travel more than that, and at most 2 mm (never more than 1 mm past the hit), so it stays a capped touch

registration.tipDiameterMm.note: the wired probe tip's outside diameter, as recorded with the 2026-10-15 bench scan: an opening must be wider than this to be entered at all

registration.tipRadiusMm.note: effective rim offset of the wired probe, from the 2026-10-15 bench scan (trace 18:59-19:03): the 38.1 mm blank read 39.5 mm wide, (39.5 - 38.1) / 2 = 0.70 mm, +/- 0.25 at a 0.5 mm step; the tip's outside diameter is 2.0 mm

registration.tipRadiusUncertaintyMm.note: the rim offset's own spread from the same 2026-10-15 bench scan: +/- 0.25 mm at a 0.5 mm step. It cancels in a centre between two walls, and doubles in a width between them

registration.viseJawResidualMm.note: provisional, not measured: the vise jaws' squareness across the jaws; #208 owes the bench measurement

registration.wiredProbeZResidualMm.note: the wired probe's repeatability in Z: five slow (F100) touches on the printed blank in the vise triggered within 0.001 mm of each other, fast (F300) within 0.004 mm and 2-6 um deep (/Z1-Firmware-Dialect.md §11.7, runbook C4, 2026-10-08)

rest.overlapMm.note: chosen, not measured: the LEAST the band both programs cut at the seam may be. The band itself is worked out per job from that job's own two cutters, and this is the floor under it — a 2 mm cutter at a 0.9 mm step-over leaves slivers 0.107 mm wide and a 0.6 mm rest cutter closes anything narrower, so the badge's pair needs about 0.493 mm. The first two-tool cut replaces this

rest.thirdToolPct.note: chosen, not measured: the share of a job's own removal area that may still be standing after both programs have run before a third cutter is suggested

run.statusReplyMs.note: chosen, not measured: how long a status poll waits for its reply; the controller answers in 0.6 to 0.7 s (#386)

runSheet.blankToleranceMm.note: chosen, not measured: how far a measured blank may differ from the job's stated size before the sheet tells the operator to change the job and regenerate

sim.budgetMs.note: chosen, not measured: the wall-clock limit one simulation load starts with. Past it the load is refused (or the worker killed), and Retry starts a load with twice this

sim.columnFlatPitchYMm.note: chosen, not measured: the flat simulation grid's Y pitch; the oracle's band grows with the cell and the sim's memory and time with 1/pitch

sim.columnPitchXMm.note: chosen, not measured: the simulation grid's X pitch; the sim's memory and time grow with 1/pitch

sim.defaultStockLengthMm.note: chosen, not measured: the blank a simulation starts with when the file states no stock, along X; 100 x 100 x 10 is the documented default (/Simulation.md §6)

sim.defaultStockThicknessMm.note: chosen, not measured: the blank a simulation starts with when the file states no stock, in Z; 100 x 100 x 10 is the documented default (/Simulation.md §6)

sim.defaultStockWidthMm.note: chosen, not measured: the blank a simulation starts with when the file states no stock, along Y; 100 x 100 x 10 is the documented default (/Simulation.md §6)

sim.playbackSpeed.note: chosen, not measured: the playback multiplier a fresh simulation session starts at, as a multiple of wall-clock time; one of 1, 5, 20 or 100

sim.rotaryPitchDeg.note: chosen, not measured: the rotary simulation grid's theta pitch; the sim's memory and time grow with 1/pitch

sim.spindleOffProximityMm.note: chosen, not measured: how close a feed move with the spindle off may come to material still present at that point, or to the bed, before it is a fault

stop.abortReplyMs.note: chosen, not measured as a bound: how long abort is given to answer (about 18 s observed on 2026-10-12, #303). The app's Stop and the bench harness's run share this one number (maintainer, 2026-10-16)

stop.idlePollMs.note: chosen, not measured: the wait between those polls; never under the 2 s status floor (#386)

stop.idlePolls.note: chosen, not measured: after abort, how many status polls look for Idle before M332; none reading Idle leaves the vacuum on and says so

tabs.count.note: chosen, not measured: holding tabs per cut-out. Four is provisional — the first part cut with tabs replaces it

tabs.heightMm.note: chosen, not measured: material a holding tab leaves below the tab top. Provisional; on a 3.81 mm badge blank it leaves 1 mm under a 2.81 mm cut

tabs.widthMm.note: chosen, not measured: holding-tab width in material. The cutter's centre path stops two tool radii further apart. Provisional until the first tabbed cut

thread.bottomClearancePitches.note: chosen, not measured: how many pitches the tool tip runs below the last full thread

thread.chordToleranceMm.note: chosen, not measured: the most a G1 chord may stray from the true helix; it sets the move count and the file size

thread.entryRampMm.note: chosen, not measured: the axial drop over which the entry ramp reaches the pass radius; 0 is a flat radial entry

thread.feed.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the helical cutting feed until a measured row replaces it

thread.pilotTipClearanceMm.note: chosen, not measured: the pilot floor must sit this far below the tool tip so the tip does not bottom

thread.plungeFeed.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the feed down the open pilot and the entry ramp until a measured row replaces it

thread.radialStepoverMm.note: chosen, not measured: the most radial depth one thread pass takes; the last pass always lands on the major radius

thread.spindleRpm.note: placeholder, not measured; not a vendor number: the thread-milling spindle speed until a measured row replaces it

tools.wearWeight.abrasive.note: chosen, not measured: a minute cutting PA-CF or PA-GF. Fibre-filled nylon is abrasive; five times plastic's wear is this app's choice (the maintainer asked for a heavier class in #456), not a bench measurement

tools.wearWeight.aluminium.note: chosen, not measured: a minute cutting 6061, 7075: three times the wear of plastic

tools.wearWeight.brass.note: chosen, not measured: a minute cutting brass: free-cutting, twice plastic

tools.wearWeight.copper.note: chosen, not measured: a minute cutting copper: gummy, as hard on a cutter as aluminium

tools.wearWeight.plastic.note: chosen, not measured: a minute cutting PLA, ABS, acrylic: the baseline

tools.wearWeight.wood.note: chosen, not measured: a minute cutting softwood, hardwood, MDF: about as hard on a cutter as plastic

vise.defaultStockProudMm.note: chosen, not measured: the cap on the stock-derived proud height; #508 derives the real proud from the seat, so this is the no-stock placeholder and the pre-#508 lower bound
